gamespot.com/articles/15-things-you-need.excerpt: Are you looking for The Blood of Dawnwalker tips? This is an open-world RPG made by the talented folks who, once upon a time, helped with the development of The Witcher 3. You can expect everything from macabre creatures and dark fantasy themes, as well as unique mechanics that are totally refreshing for the genre. Of course, it goes without saying that things can get a tad bit confusing at first, which is why our guide aims to assist you for the long road ahead. You’re a Dawnwalker - A part-human, part-vampire hybrid In The Blood of Dawnwalker, you play as Coen, a commoner from a small village called Laslea Glen. Circumstances have not only caused Coen’s family to get kidnapped by vampire lords known as vrakhiri. He’s also been turned into a monstrosity--a dawnwalker--someone who lives as a human by day and turns into a vampire at night. This dynamic changes how you approach the game. During the day, you heal up normally by eating food and you chat with shopkeepers who ply their craft in settlements. You may also cast Witchcraft spells and commune with the spirits of the dead. You’re basically a warrior-spellcaster with the limitations of being human. Just a medieval warrior hunting for wolves. Learn to manage your bloodthirst as a vampire Things change drastically at night. As a vampire, you need to satisfy your bloodthirst. This means feeding on hapless stragglers and wildlife. If your health is too low and you approach a person, you might lose control, causing you to bleed them dry as you feast. That said, being a lord of the night has its perks. You get to use serrated claws to strike foes. You get to teleport across short distances. And, yes, you can even walk vertically on walls, defying gravity and all that is holy. gamespot.com/articles/final-fantasy-reso.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Is A Return To Classic Series Conventions While Also Evolving Square Enix’s HD-2D Style
gamespot.com/articles/final-fantasy-reso.excerpt: Given its rich legacy spanning almost four decades, it's something of a surprise that Square Enix has taken its time to give Final Fantasy an outing in HD-2D, the retro-modern aesthetic that clearly harks back to the pinnacle of pixel art from RPG classics of the 16-bit era, including Final Fantasy VI. But rather than introduce this visual style to the franchise with a brand-new title, Square Enix is using the HD-2D treatment to reimagine and preserve a now-defunct mobile game. Final Fantasy Resonance is a reimagining of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius that's similar in scope to Octopath Traveler 0, an enhanced console adaptation for Octopath Traveler: Champions of the Continent. Although Final Fantasy Resonance is a retelling of Brave Exvius's first season, casting you in the role of Rain along with party members Lasswell, Fina, and Lid, the mobile title was played with just touch controls, and so there's naturally been an overhaul to the control system to suit a console experience. But from hands-on at Gamescom 2026 plenty more has been overhauled and added to transform this from the mobile game's streamlined structure and limited exploration into something you would expect from a classic Final Fantasy title that can be enjoyed at a leisurely pace, including traversing an overworld map, where you can also summon a chocobo for getting around. At a glance, the turn-based battle system shares some similarities with Octopath Traveler, with a timeline at the top showing the order of party members and enemies' turns, as well as a stagger system, albeit not like that series' puzzle of chipping away at enemy weaknesses. But being a Final Fantasy game, it has many of the series' classic tropes too. gamespot.com/articles/epic-games-new-voi.excerpt: Epic Games has announced that it's going to make it easier than ever to hang out and talk with friends across different platforms by launching Epic Parties. This voice chat service will work across Fortnite (on all supported platforms), the Epic Games Store launcher (PC, iOS, and Android), and the Epic Games app (iOS and Android). For example, you can start a voice party from your phone or PC launcher, ring up a friend who is busy playing Fortnite on their PlayStation, and even transfer that call from your phone to your PC when you get back to your desk. This means that you can sit in on a voice call through the Epic PC Launcher while playing completely different games from your Epic library. Other benefits include a seamless approach to grouping friends together, as Epic says that if you're in a voice party with friends and everyone decides to open Fortnite, then the game will automatically drop you all into the same lobby together. This new feature is competing directly with Discord, which has been the go-to third-party app for users for several years. Epic's built-in alternative aims to let users bring their social list, voice channels, and digital avatar with them across multiple platforms and from game to game, whether you are on iOS, Android, PC, or console. Epic has also hinted that these voice and avatar systems will be integrated directly into Unreal Engine 6, and the tools will be offered to other developers in time. For now, it's currently rolling out to Fortnite, and Epic Parties will be available in Rocket League next year. According to Epic's year-in-review stats , over $1 billion was spent in the store in 2025, and it reached an all-time record of 78 million monthly active users on PC. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-fishing-and-.title: GTA 6 Fishing And Hunting Doesn’t Work Like You Think It Does
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-fishing-and-.excerpt: Rockstar Games has confirmed new details about how fishing and hunting work in GTA 6, and it's probably not what you would expect. Speaking to YouTuber TGG , Rockstar North's Rob Nelson confirmed that fishing in GTA 6 is limited to catch and release--players cannot keep any fish. Why? "It didn't fit this game," Nelson said, adding that fishing in GTA 6 is mainly for fun. Players can also complete fishing-related challenges and amass collectibles. Jason fishing in GTA 6. In Rockstar's last game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II, players could catch a great assortment of fish and then cook and eat them. That made sense given the time period of the game, that being 1899. GTA 6 is set in modern times, and main characters Jason and Lucia, like you and me, have access to numerous food options at any given time. Eating food in GTA 6 will make you gain weight, and players can use the excess calories to bulk up at the gym. As for hunting in GTA 6, Nelson said the game's hunting system is one of many ways in the game that players can make money . The hunting system is unlocked through a friend that knows Jason, but TGG theorized that this person has not been shown yet in any GTA 6 footage so far. In addition to catching fish and killing animals, players will be able to "inspect" the creatures, borrowing a system from Red Dead Redemption 2. GTA 6 also has dogs that you can pet, scold (you monster), and inspect . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. gamespot.com/articles/metro-2039-kicks-o.excerpt: During today's State of Play , 4A Games revealed new PS5 Pro footage of Metro 2039 and finally confirmed the game's release date. Narrowing down from a previously known February 2027 release window, it's now confirmed that the game will be out on February 4 of next year. That means it's currently the first high-profile AAA game launch in a month that will be full of them. In the weeks after Metro 2039's launch, we can expect the likes of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, God of War Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Fable to all come out. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rxfWaSg_-hc The new gameplay footage looked great, which makes me thankful that Metro 2039 is arriving before all those other titles. The three-minute State of Play trailer begins with The Stranger slowly exploring the remnants of a dentist's office. He discovers that some Novoreich forces are there in the apartments above, and a shootout ensues. The YouTube video description for the trailer reveals that this footage is meant to highlight the "environmental detail, kinetic combat, and the technological advances that have been made" for this new Metro game. The video description also reveals why the footage looks so good: It was captured on PS5 Pro, on which Metro 2039 has a 60fps performance mode that supports ray tracing at a 4K resolution. That performance mode will even be available on the base PS5 and Xbox Series X models, with 4A Games touting that Metro 2039 is "the first game in the series to be built from the ground up for ray tracing." gamespot.com/articles/jin-sakai-returns-.excerpt: Today, during the PlayStation State of Play livestream , Sucker Punch offered a look at Ghost of Yotei's upcoming roguelike mode, Most Wanted. The mode will feature four playable characters, and Yotei's Atsu, Oyuki, and Nagato will be joined by a familar face from the past: The Ghost of Tsushima, Jin Sakai, will officially return. Most Wanted, which the trailer calls a "combat survival mode," lets players choose one of the four samurai, each with their own weapons and abilities, to take them on a hunt for one of the Yotei Six. Each of the Six, if defeated, will offer a reward of coins that can then be spent to upgrade the samurai for future runs. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nlchabfwy_w A new post on the official PlayStation Blog further explores the new mode, saying that the core of the mode lies in its Perks system. "As you progress through a run, you’ll frequently select between new perks including weapon mastery, gear loadouts, summons, parries, survivability, and more," the blog says. "These are the cornerstone of crafting the perfect build and lead to some of the most exciting surprises as you find the challenge or unexpected value that comes from mixing and matching perks. This new mode marks the first time Jin Sakai returns as a playable characters since his starring role in 2020's Ghost of Tsushima. The PS Blog post says that the development team made sure to "take his Ghost of Tsushima model and keep it faithful while also applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei," as he can use all four of his fighting stances from Ghost of Tsushima, as well as sticky bombs, the Dance of Wrath, and his Ghost stance. Ghost of Yotei's Echoes of Sekigahara expansion, as well as the Most Wanted roguelike mode, launch October 1. Players who own the base game can purchase a Complete Edition upgrade with the extra content, while new players can purchase Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition with all content in one package.

gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-trai.title: Resident Evil Trailer Shows The Sequence Where Its Star Almost Died For Real
gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-trai.excerpt: During the September 3 State of Play , Sony debuted a new clip from the upcoming Resident Evil movie, and it was both dark and hilarious. That should be no surprise, as comedy and horror are naturally intertwined, and the movie is written and directed by sketch comedy veteran Zach Cregger. In the clip, we see Austin Abrams' character, the medical courier Bryan, running down a street in Raccoon City as zombies throw themselves off rooftops trying to catch him. They explode on impact, with blood flying everywhere. Bryan screams as he runs down the street amidst the carnage, uttering some hilarious noises and guttural screams. Check out the new footage below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KGlapnJFacE Cregger wanted to film this sequence practically instead of using CGI. The production team created 150-pound “body-sized blood bags” that were dropped from cranes to create the effect. One of the blood bags came close to striking Abrams, and Cregger said, “It would’ve killed him.” Bryan, according to Cregger, is an "idiot" who finds himself in a horrifying situation and is just trying to survive. The entire movie feels like “one gigantic sequence,” Cregger said, adding that things begin to “pop off” five minutes into the movie–and it only ramps up from there. “It feels like one gigantic sequence,” he says. “Things pop off about five minutes in and it basically stays like that until the end. What I love about the games is that you move from set-piece to set-piece. Every location has a unique challenge. So again, I’m borrowing from the games directly in that rhythm, where you’re just running through a gauntlet.” The Resident Evil movie releases on September 18, and it's expected to have the biggest opening ever for a Resident Evil movie .

gamespot.com/articles/mmos-have-stagnate.title: MMOs Have “Stagnated,” Guild Wars 3 Studio Head Says
gamespot.com/articles/mmos-have-stagnate.excerpt: Guild Wars 3 developer ArenaNet wants to try "wild, crazy ideas" in a genre that, according to its studio head, has "stagnated" in recent years. During a hands-off demo where early Guild Wars 3 gameplay was shown to members of the press, I asked ArenaNet studio head Colin Johanson about the state of the MMO genre in 2026 and what problems Guild Wars 3 is looking to solve. He had plenty to say on the subject. Many MMO players are still playing the same games they were 10-20 years ago, Johanson said, citing decade-old (or older) examples like World of Warcraft, The Elder Scrolls Online, Final Fantasy 14, and, of course, ArenaNet's own Guild Wars 2. In that same time, "minute-to-minute gameplay in MMOs has stagnated," even as other genres have modernized and become more approachable, he said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ITPzxITngqA That's "really good timing" for ArenaNet and Guild Wars 3, Johanson said, and one that presents a big opportunity for a new game to break in and shake up the scene. "There's been very little new in the last decade, and a lot of those [newer] games either don't exist anymore or were canceled in development before they made their way out," Johanson said. "We see MMO fans constantly clamoring for and asking for something new and saying this genre desperately needs something new to move it forward right now." Johanson certainly has a point. Set in a wartorn Soviet city, empty of people but littered with tanks wearing coats of Frankensteined cattle corpses (light stuff!), Carcass Clad is a three-player co-op experience that shares the stressful responsibility of piloting a tank and taking down enemy units between those unlucky three. If you read the name Wrong Organ and thought, ‘Wait, the Mouthwashing team? They're making a multiplayer co-op game?’, I can't fault your surprise. Edwin did interview them about it back in June , but I walked up to the booth knowing the devs themselves and little more, so I was experiencing all of Carcass Clad and its heavy departure from their previous work for the first time.
